look_here_first: WITCHGRASS: Warm-season HAIRY ANNUAL. Find distinct coarse/papillose-based hairs along the sheaths and nodes BELOW an enormous airy irregular many-branch panicle. The ripe ~2–4 mm spikelets sit at tips of extraordinarily slender stems. Confirm annual fibrous rootstock and one measured spikelet with shorter lower glume. Seedhead shape alone will NOT distinguish similarly open Panicum grasses.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Kew/POWO accepts Panicum capillare, describes it as an annual, and lists Texas in its native range. Hagenbuch & Lemke explicitly record Hays County (Breckenridge 518, SWT). UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed Williamson County treatment. USDA ARS Biocollections specimen NA0083935 records Bell County, Texas, Belton Dam Site.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Occurrence is not treated as nativity; introduced records do not count toward the three-county native threshold.

crew_field_check: WITCHGRASS: Warm-season HAIRY ANNUAL. Find distinct coarse/papillose-based hairs along the sheaths and nodes BELOW an enormous airy irregular many-branch panicle. The ripe ~2–4 mm spikelets sit at tips of extraordinarily slender stems. Confirm annual fibrous rootstock and one measured spikelet with shorter lower glume. Seedhead shape alone will NOT distinguish similarly open Panicum grasses.

P. hallii = smaller stiff blue-green perennial bunch; P. coloratum = introduced African perennial tough knotty tuft; P. virgatum = larger rhizomatous switchgrass with a white blade-base collar-hair triangle. Witchgrass alone is the hairy annual with huge diffuse panicle.
Examine the same plant's crown, collar and mature spikelet with a millimeter scale before assigning difficult specimens.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Panicum hallii: Witchgrass is annual, hairy, and has a huge diffuse panicle; Hall's is a perennial glaucous bunchgrass with a smaller stiff-branched panicle. Dichanthelium spp.: Witchgrass is annual and lacks the characteristic spring/fall rosette-grass flowering pattern.

field_id_lesson.look_here_first: Witchgrass: annual with coarse tubercle-based sheath hairs and an extremely diffuse, many-branched mature panicle; confirm mature spikelets rather than identifying from panicle silhouette alone.

measured_checks.sheath: Conspicuously hairy, often tubercle-based; inspect nodes and collar.
measured_checks.panicle: Large and diffuse, branches spreading widely at maturity.
measured_checks.spikelets: Small and awnless; measure individual mature spikelet with mm scale.
measured_checks.glumes: Lower glume much shorter than spikelet; verify relative lengths.
measured_checks.lemma: Inspect fertile upper floret under magnification.

lookalikes: Panicum hallii: perennial, glaucous, stiff basal foliage and smaller panicle.
Panicum coloratum: perennial forage grass, knotty crown and generally less chaotic panicle.
Panicum virgatum: taller perennial switchgrass; crown and mature spikelets differ.
photo_gaps: Measured spikelet with lower glume and fertile lemma

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Witchgrass: airy panicle, hairy sheath, then real spikelet parts
steps: Start with the Matt Lavin whole diffuse-panicle image (gallery panel 3). Identify long slender branches and small distant spikelets without counting glumes from this scale.
Use Harry Rose's same-species foliage/culm view (panel 4) followed by Matt Lavin's hairy sheath/collar-region view (panel 5). The TRUE ligule is not yet clearly isolated or measured.

Study Stefan.lefnaer's original labelled spikelet dissection (panel 2): glumes, sterile versus fertile lemmas, and fertile palea. These are photographer-labelled source parts, not new assistant arrows or a vouchered same-plant Texas collection.
Compare the physical CC0 tiny spikelet photo (panel 1) with the DIFFERENT SPECIES Panicum hallii photograph (panel 6); never transfer photo-derived claims between the two species.
For a finished local card, photograph a rooted entire annual, an opened true ligule with 1-mm bar, and intact/dissected mature spikelets from the SAME determined Texas individual.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Two actual JPEGs are archived in GitHub; four source photos remain remote-only. Do not claim complete physical archive or a measured ligule. Existing labelled external dissection is useful but not a Hays County same-plant voucher.
